title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: which counted withdrawals of a reconciled cycle each need an excess withdrawal fee
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which overdraft protection transfers have been made, when the excess withdrawal fees of a statement cycle are reconciled. It turns the number of withdrawals that count toward the allowance into the number of withdrawals that each need an excess withdrawal fee of their own.

## Policy clause

The counted withdrawals over and above the tier's withdrawal allowance per cycle each need an excess withdrawal fee of their own, taken as none when there are none. A tier whose allowance is unlimited has none.

## Order of the calculation

1. If the tier's allowance is unlimited, no withdrawal needs a fee; stop.
2. Take the number of counted withdrawals less the allowance.
3. If that difference is below zero, take zero.

The counted withdrawals that need a fee are the ones past the allowance in posting order: with an allowance of 3, the 4th, 5th and later counted withdrawals.

## Worked cases (hypothetical tier: allowance 3; illustrative, not a tier value)

| Counted withdrawals in the cycle | Less the allowance | Withdrawals that each need a fee |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | below zero | 0 |
| 3 | 0 | 0 |
| 5 | 2 | 2 (the 4th and the 5th) |
| any number, on a tier with an unlimited allowance | not applicable | 0 |

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "Withdrawals exactly at the allowance leave one withdrawal needing a fee." **Correct basis:** only withdrawals over and above the allowance need a fee; at the allowance the difference is zero.

**Does the per-cycle maximum on excess withdrawal fees reduce this number?** No; this number counts the withdrawals that need a fee. How many fees may still be charged in the cycle is a separate figure.
